key_insight: A unified framework couples a forward predictive model with an inverse generative model to design liquid electrolytes, producing three high-conductivity candidates that were experimentally validated.
problem_solved: Accelerates and automates electrolyte formulation by enabling reliable prediction of properties and targeted generation of new candidate mixtures, reducing trial-and-error and experimental cost.
method: Train a forward predictive surrogate to map electrolyte compositions and conditions to target properties (e.g., ionic conductivity).
Use an inverse generative model guided by the predictor to propose candidate formulations that optimize target properties.
Close the loop with experimental validation of top candidates and retrain/update models for improved accuracy and robustness.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for integrating predictive and generative ML for materials design, demonstrating how closed-loop AI can produce experimentally validated candidates and speed up discovery in chemistry and battery research.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram showing forward predictor → evaluation → inverse generator → experimental validation loop
Conductivity landscape or heatmap over composition space with highlighted generated candidates
Latent-space or embedding plot illustrating how generated formulations differ from training set
Bar chart comparing predicted vs. measured conductivity for the validated candidates
paper_title: A unified predictive and generative solution for liquid electrolyte formulation
paper_authors: Zhenze Yang, Yifan Wu, Xu Han, Ziqing Zhang, Haoen Lai
